name: Richard III of England
summary: Richard III took the throne in 1483 on the claim that Edward IV's children were illegitimate, and defended it against the rebellions of 1483 and Henry Tudor's invasion. His only Parliament (1484) passed Titulus Regius and reforms to bail, juries and benevolences, though how far he personally drove them is unclear. Little of his own political thought survives beyond his title claim and proclamations.
